short: Johan Banér's decisive victory restored Swedish prestige and military capability in northern Germany following the disaster at Nördlingen.
full:
Fought on 4 October 1636, the Battle of Wittstock pitted a diminished Swedish army under Johan Banér and Alexander Leslie against a significantly larger combined Imperial and Saxon force. Facing numerical inferiority and the potential collapse of the Swedish position in Germany, Banér executed a risky double envelopment.

Leslie led a lengthy flanking maneuver through difficult terrain while Banér held the Imperial center. The delayed arrival of the flanking force nearly cost the Swedes the battle, but their eventual strike into the Imperial rear triggered a complete collapse of the enemy army. The victory shattered the Saxon military, restored Sweden's dominance in the north, and proved their army remained lethal even without French support.
